title: Quantifying Social Biases in NLP: A Generalization and Empirical Comparison of Extrinsic Fairness Metrics
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured systemic differences in model performance (bias) for sentiment analysis and named entity recognition tasks on text that explicitly mentions different religious identity terms. This was quantified using a variety of fairness metrics.
findings: The paper found statistically significant evidence of unintended bias related to religion in the models tested. The performance on sentiment analysis tasks differed across various religious groups, and the magnitude of the measured bias varied depending on the specific fairness metric used. For example, tests showed very low p-values (e.g., 1.14 x 10^-23), indicating that the observed differences in model behavior across religious groups were highly unlikely to be due to chance.
